# .github

## What it is

`.github/` holds the repo's GitHub Actions surface: eight workflows under
`workflows/` (`ci.yml`, `ci-rerun.yml`, `ci-app.yml`, `release.yml`,
`release-app.yml`, `update-model-pricing.yml`, `audit-branch-protection.yml`,
`refresh-test-durations.yml`), the release-notes label map (`release.yml` at
this level — not the workflow of the same name), and the issue/PR
templates ([[issue-intake.ava.okf.md]]).

GitHub-hosted runners: general CI and operational automation use
`ubuntu-24.04`, while app CI / release also use macOS 14 and Windows 2022. No self-hosted fleet, `container:`, or runner provisioner. Public-repo hosted minutes let the same CI
lane run for the canonical repo and forks without repository gating.

Each job provisions its own toolchain inline (uv, Node 22, Postgres 17 + Redis
server binaries on PATH, Playwright chromium), because a hosted runner starts
bare. The suite needs the pg/redis *server binaries* only: it spins throwaway
native clusters itself (`tests/_containers.py`).

## Core responsibilities

### `workflows/ci.yml` — the whole gate

Triggers: `pull_request` (every PR, no path filtering), `push` to `main`
(with `paths-ignore` for `ava_builtins/skills/**` and `**/*.md`), and
`workflow_dispatch`. Concurrency is keyed on the ref and cancels in-progress
runs for pull requests only, so a force-push supersedes its own earlier run
while main keeps every run.

Sharded fan-out behind three stable check names, every job capped by
`timeout-minutes` so a hang cannot run to GitHub's global limit. A `classify`
job maps the PR diff through `shared/repo_change.py` (the selective-restart
classifier) and gates the suites: docs-only skips everything, frontend-only
skips backend, backend-only skips the frontend unit suite; e2e runs whenever
either side changed. Draft PRs skip CI until ready_for_review — except
Trunk test branches (`trunk-merge/*`, `trunk-temp/*`), which must verify.

[[test-selection.ava.okf.md]] covers informational selection; see
[conventions/test-selection.md](../conventions/test-selection.md).

The required Gitleaks job scans the complete Git history and working tree on
every eligible run, including docs-only changes; `.gitleaks.toml` is also the
local pre-commit policy, so fixture exceptions have one owner. A separate
dependency-audit job runs `uv audit --frozen` and `npm audit` as informational
checks while the remediation policy matures; its failure does not block the
workflow yet.

| Check name (protection + queue) | Composition |
|---|---|
| backend (pytest + pyright) | aggregator over `backend-static` (ruff, migration + clock-lattice lints, migration smoke, pyright) + 12 pytest-split shards (`-n 4` each, least_duration (LPT)-balanced via the committed `.test_durations`, refreshed nightly by `.github/workflows/refresh-test-durations.yml`); combines per-shard coverage and applies the 85% line gate |
| frontend (eslint + tsc + vitest) | one job: `npm ci`, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint `--max-warnings 0`, `vitest run --coverage`, serial flaky lane |
| e2e (Playwright happy path) | aggregator over 4 shards, Playwright chromium `-n 2` each (browser dir cached) |

Postgres/Redis install is a composite action (`.github/actions/install-pg-redis`)
with cached apt archives and timeout+retry — infrastructure steps retry, tests
never do.

Both `backend` and `e2e` point `AVA_DB_URL` / `AVA_REDIS_URL` at unreachable
sentinel ports: the suite must provision its own throwaway cluster, and a
sentinel turns "a test quietly reached a real data plane" into a connection
error instead of a silent pass.

### `workflows/refresh-test-durations.yml` — nightly shard timing refresh

[[refresh-test-durations.ava.okf.md]] describes the isolated measurement and
review-only publication loop.

### `workflows/release.yml` — tag to GitHub Release

A dated three-segment tag push (`v<major>.<minor>.<patch>-<YYYYMMDD>`) creates a
GitHub Release whose body is the annotated tag's own message. `scripts/release_cut.py`
writes that annotation (the day's PRs, categorized by conventional-commit type),
so there is no separate release-notes authoring step. Re-pushing a tag is
idempotent — `gh release create` warns and exits 0 when the release exists.

### `workflows/ci-app.yml` — path-filtered native app gate

Changes under `ui/app/` or the app release/test tooling run Rust format,
desktop clippy on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, an `aarch64` debug APK build after
applying the generated-project overlay, and the Android-overlay + updater-manifest
pytest files. The path filter keeps unrelated backend/frontend changes from
installing Tauri's native toolchain.

### `workflows/release-app.yml` — cross-platform app release

An `app-v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` tag builds a universal macOS DMG and Windows
NSIS installer. Complete secret groups activate Apple, Windows, and Tauri
updater signing; missing groups retain unsigned
build evidence. Signed updater archives become `latest.json`, published both
with the immutable version release and at the stable `app-latest` feed asset.
Manual dispatch builds without publishing.

### `release.yml` — release-notes label map

Config, not a workflow: it maps PR labels to sections for GitHub's
auto-generated release notes. The primary path is the tag annotation above; this
is the fallback for a release that opts into `generate_release_notes` instead.

### Action pinning

Every `uses:` is pinned to a **commit SHA** with the human-readable version in a
trailing comment. A moving tag like `@v6` is a mutable pointer the action's owner
can repoint at any time, which is a supply-chain write into every CI run.
`dependabot.yml` watches the `github-actions` ecosystem weekly so the pins are
updated by a reviewable PR rather than drifting silently or going stale.

### Repository automation and external-state audits

CI reruns, official-price proposals, and the weekly branch-protection drift loop
are detailed in [[repository-automation.ava.okf.md]].

## Key dependencies

- [[../tests/tests.ava.okf.md]] — the suite the CI gates run.
- [[../scripts/scripts.ava.okf.md]] — `ci_utils.py` polls a PR's CI to a verdict;
  release scripts create cluster notes and the app updater manifest; the branch
  audit compares GitHub's live protection state with `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- [[../ui/app/app.ava.okf.md]] — native app built and released by the two
  app workflows.
- The hosted runner image supplies the base OS; everything Ava-specific is
  installed by the job's own steps, so a CI change never depends on out-of-band
  host state.

## Entry points

- Events: `pull_request`, `push` to main (`paths-ignore` for general CI and
  `paths` for app CI), `workflow_dispatch`, dated cluster release tags, and
  `app-v*` app release tags, plus the daily model-pricing and weekly
  branch-protection schedules.
- Manual full run: `workflow_dispatch` on `ci.yml`.
- Local equivalent before pushing: `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files` plus
  `.venv/bin/pytest tests/<area>` — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Notes

- **The workflow steps are the gate, not a superset of local hooks.** The
  pre-commit config carries roughly 25 lint hooks; `ci.yml` runs the subset
  named above. A hook that exists only in pre-commit is enforced only for
  contributors who installed it, so anything that must hold for every PR belongs
  in the workflow.
- `paths-ignore` applies to `push` only; pull requests are gated by the
  `classify` job instead (change-class granularity, never per-test path
  selection — a `shared/` one-liner can break `tests/gateway/`, so a touched
  suite always runs whole).
- Job names are surfaced to reviewers as check names; renaming one silently
  changes what a branch-protection rule matches.
